column1: # THE GATE MANIFEST: one row per way the repository runs a gate script, and the one place that says so.
# Before this file the CI workflow (.github/workflows/lean_action_ci.yml) was the de facto list of
# gates, scripts/tests/ci_gate_inventory.txt a hand-kept copy of commands extracted from it, the
# Makefile a third list, and check_gate_registration.sh a fourth (its SKIP table). Each could drift
# from the others. Now the facts live here, and the copies are generated from it:
#   scripts/tests/ci_gate_inventory.txt   the `cmd` of every `via=step` row, LC_ALL=C sorted, unique
#   mk/gates.mk                           a .PHONY make target per row with a `make` cell, included from the
#   .github/workflows/lean_action_ci.yml  the steps inside each `# BEGIN GENERATED: gates <job> from
#                                         `- name: <step>` / `run: <cmd>` step per gen=y row, from row
#                                         <id> on in manifest order, until a gen=n row of the job or the
#                                         job's next block; the rest of the workflow is hand-written
# python3 scripts/gen/gates.py --write regenerates them; --check fails when one is stale or a row is
# invalid. check_gate_registration.sh runs --check, fails on any scripts/tests/{check,test,run}_*.sh,
# scripts/tests/check_*.py or scripts/ci/*.sh without a row, and cross-checks `via` against its
# reachability walk of the workflow and the scripts it calls.
# ADDING A GATE: add its row here, run `python3 scripts/gen/gates.py --write`, and, for a CI step,
# either set gen=y and place the row inside a generated block of its job (the generator writes the
# step), or write the step in the workflow by hand with gen=n, in the same commit.
# FORMAT: tab-separated, one row per line after the column line below; every cell is non-empty, `-`
# meaning "none" or "not recorded yet". ORDER: rows with a job come first, in workflow order (job,
# then step, then the cmd's position in the step), because a generated block writes its steps in
# manifest order; the rows with no job follow, sorted by id (LC_ALL=C).
#   id      unique row name: lowercase letters, digits and '-'; derived from the script name, plus its
#           arguments or environment when one script runs several ways
#   cmd     the command as the workflow spells it for a CI step (the inventory line: what
#           run_ci_gates_local.sh's extraction reads, so step `env:` and a VAR="..." prefix whose
#           value holds spaces are not part of it), else the plain way to run it
#           (`bash scripts/tests/x.sh`); it names exactly one script
#   job     the workflow job that runs it (the key under `jobs:`), or `-` when no CI step does
#   step    that job's step name as GitHub shows it (the YAML value; an unquoted ` #` ends it), or `-`
#             step              a workflow step runs `cmd`; it is in the inventory and the local full
#             ci-only:<reason>  a workflow step runs `cmd`, but the local full run does not run this
#                               form of it (run_ci_gates_local.sh's extraction exclusions, or a step
#                               env the extraction cannot see); not in the inventory
#             agg:<script>      run by <script> (scripts/tests, scripts/ci or scripts/gen), which CI
#                               reaches; the reachability walk must see that edge
#             skip:<reason>     CI never runs it, for the stated reason; the walk must NOT reach it,
#                               so a skip that stops being true is reported as stale
#   area    the compiler area the gate covers, from the stage vocabulary of docs/bugs/area_map.tsv:
#           Parse Resolve Check Elab Mono Lower SSA EmitSSA EmitLLVM Interp Proof Report Std CLI
#   owner   who answers for the gate when it goes red (a name or team token), `-` until assigned
#   claim   one line: what a pass establishes (seeded from the Makefile `##` text, else the script's
#           header comment); for a make row it is the target's `make help` text, so no `##`
#             prepush   the pre-push hook runs it on every push (an unindented, uncommented
#             pr        CI's landing tier: every push to main and every pull request, except that a
#                       label-gated job (multi-kernel) runs on a pull request only with its label;
#                       the hook may select it from the diff (scripts/tests/select_gates.sh)
#             campaign  only in CI's campaign tier (workflow_dispatch with campaign=true, nightly), or
#                       by hand for a campaign-class harness
#             manual    only when someone runs it (a make target or by hand)
#             skip      not run at all (with via=skip:<reason>)
#   spec    comma-separated live keys of docs/spec/ids.tsv the gate enforces, or `-`
#   make    the make target that runs exactly `cmd`, or `-`; unique across rows, never also written by
#           hand in the Makefile (targets whose recipe is not one plain gate command stay there)
#   shell   the nix devshell it runs in: gates (`nix develop .#gates`, or the default shell) or provers
#   build   y when it needs the compiler built (`.lake/build/bin/concrete`), else n; a make row with y
#   gen     y when gates.py generates this row's workflow step (a two-line `- name:` / `run:` step
#           inside a generated block of its job; via must be step), else n: a step with `if:`, `env:`,
#           more than one command, a preceding comment, or a name GitHub cuts short at ` #` stays
#   kind    the test taxonomy of a test-suite row (later slices); `-` for a gate
# WHY `kind` IS A COLUMN AND NOT A DIRECTORY LAYOUT: classifying tests by moving files (tests/unit,
# tests/integration, ...) would rewrite paths that 293 files reference under tests/ (fixtures named
# by gates, goldens, bug records, docs). A column classifies the same tests with no path churn, and
# a later move stays possible once one owner resolves those paths.
